tasks_completed.description: Fix --day flag parser bug in generate-and-deploy.sh
tasks_completed.changes: Added 'shift' immediately after 'PLAN_ID="$1"' on line 35 to consume the positional plan-id argument; changed 'while [ "$#" -gt 1 ]' to 'while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]' on line 40 so the option loop processes the remaining args including a possible trailing --day argv.
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause was that the option parser used 'while [ "$#" -gt 1 ]' AND 'case "$1"' with no prior shift, so $1 remained the plan-id ('test-plan-id', etc.) which fell through to the '*) Unknown option' catch-all and exited 1. Fix: shift past the plan-id first, then loop while args remain (>0).

git_rationale.root_cause_commit: unknown (parser logic predates available history window for this fix)
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: Original parser pattern assumed 'while [ "$#" -gt 1 ]' was a guard against running off the end, but combined with 'case "$1"' and no leading shift, $1 still pointed at the positional plan-id during the first iteration, causing the catch-all branch to reject it.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: shift consumes the positional plan-id BEFORE the option loop, so $1 inside the loop is always an option flag (or empty). The loop bound is corrected to >0 so a trailing --day in odd-arg-count invocations is still processed.

dev.qa_notes: Run AC6 verification: (1) `bash scripts/generate-and-deploy.sh <plan-id> --day 1-5` must NOT print 'Unknown option <plan-id>' and must NOT exit 1 at the parser stage. (2) `bash -x scripts/generate-and-deploy.sh china-20260412-092624 --force --day 1-5 2>&1 | grep fetch-images-batch` must show '--day 1-5' in the python invocation line. (3) Existing flag combinations (no flags, --force only, --force --day, --day only, --bogus rejection) must all behave correctly with no regression.

self_verification.build: pass (bash -n scripts/generate-and-deploy.sh has no syntax errors implicit in successful invocations)
self_verification.notes: Verified all 5 flag-combination cases plus downstream --day forwarding via bash -x trace. No regressions.
